target_customer: Enterprises and teams wanting Dropbox-style file sync on their own infrastructure
problem: Cloud file sync stored data on vendor servers, which security-conscious organizations could not accept.
business_model: enterprise software license/subscription with a free tier for small teams
product_category: private cloud file sync and collaboration

founders.name: Yuri Sagalov
founders.background_notes: Later a YC partner 2014 to 2019, then General Catalyst; became CEO of Redbooth after the merger.

competitors.name: Dropbox
competitors.what: cloud file sync; AeroFS was pitched as Dropbox that runs inside the firewall

technical_complexity.rationale: Peer to peer encrypted sync across platforms without a central cloud, run on customer infrastructure, was hard for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: On-premises control fit security-driven buyers and created deployment lock-in, but Dropbox and Box could address security concerns.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents moved into enterprise features; AeroFS later merged into Redbooth rather than being bought by them.

market_need_then: Enterprise concern about storing data on third-party cloud servers; TechCrunch in 2011 framed AeroFS as the private-network answer to Dropbox.

branding.domain_note: aerofs.com now redirects to a GoDaddy for-sale page, so the domain lapsed after the company ended.

identity.voice_and_tone: Dropbox-like user experience with private security positioning

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by TechCrunch and Computerworld; no merch or fan evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear product framing in press but little evidence of brand recognition beyond tech press; name resembles unrelated Aero brands.

outcome_analysis: AeroFS was a Summer 2010 YC company selling a private-cloud Dropbox alternative to enterprises. It raised a reported 10 million dollar Series B in 2015 and later combined with Redbooth as Air Computing merged with it, with Yuri Sagalov becoming CEO. Deal date and terms were not found, so the reason is not fully public.
notes: YC status Acquired, but a search result describes a merger of Air Computing (AeroFS) with Redbooth; recorded as merger. Series B lead investor conflicts across sources (Avalon Ventures in one). A 5.5M Series A appears on one aggregator only and is unverified, not recorded. YC investor list: Avalon Ventures, a16z Seed, Y Combinator, SV Angel, Lowercase Capital, Maynard Webb, Jerry Yang, Paul Buchheit. Competitor source is 2011-09 press; Dropbox already existed at the 2010 batch.
